reason: The skin-cell picture shows how the body's surface is continually replaced, matching the first goal.
expectation: The body model should show new skin cells replacing those shed at the surface.

effect: The skin replacement goal is complete; I can now work on replacement red blood cells.
reaction: The result clearly showed new cells moving up as old ones shed.
reason: The marrow picture shows developing red cells, and the blood supplies the materials they need.
expectation: The supplied marrow cells should produce replacement red blood cells.

effect: The marrow cells are developing into red cells, and the new goal is to connect blood renewal with skin renewal.
reaction: The time strip makes it clear that red cells mature in the marrow.
reason: The new goal suggests bringing the developing red cells together with the body renewing its skin.
expectation: The body model should show both skin and red blood cell renewal.

effect: Skin and blood renewal are connected; the new goal is to renew bone.
reaction: It is interesting that replacement continues in the completed body.
reason: The pictures show one kind of cell removing old bone and another laying down new material, matching the new goal.
expectation: Together the cells should show a small patch of old bone being replaced.

effect: The cells must work on the body rather than combine directly; the old bone patch is now being cleared.
reaction: The compatibility hint clarified the order after my guess did not work.
reason: The bone-forming cells lay down new material, so they should complete the cleared patch.
expectation: New bone material should be laid down in the cleared patch.

effect: The cleared bone patch now has new material, completing the bone-renewal goal and the chapter.
reaction: Seeing the same person move while the insets showed ongoing renewal made the ending clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing skin and blood renewal together was worthwhile because it showed that the body keeps replacing cells even after it has been built.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the developing red cells to the body felt mostly like an assembly step; the marrow result had already shown where they mature.

surprise.text: I was surprised that bone is renewed in small patches while the rest of the skeleton stays in place.

arbitrary.text: I expected the bone-removing and bone-forming cells to combine directly. The hint showed that removal had to be connected to the body first, but the required order was not obvious to me.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter explored a new process. The connections between the finished body and ongoing renewal were interesting, though some assembly steps felt predictable.
